title: SkySearch Hosted API - Embeddings + Rerank Demo
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked SkySearch through the Hosted API embeddings and rerank endpoints, showed Console usage and Optimize recommendations. Discussed integration patterns, latency vs cost tradeoffs, privacy/VPC concerns, and benchmarking next steps. Action items include PoC benchmark, security docs, and pricing proposal.
transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2028-07-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Head of Search, SkySearch), Elena Garcia (Principal ML Engineer), Tom O'Brien (CTO)
---
SUMMARY (auto-generated): Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + rerank. Showed sample integration, Console metrics, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. Customer asked about VPC/private infra, SOC2, and run book for benchmarking.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - this is Maya from Redwood, and with me is Liam, our SE. How's it going, Raj?
[00:18] Raj: Good, thanks. Excited to see the embeddings + rerank flow. We've been evaluating Pinecone and Weaviate, and also doing some in-house with Elastic.
[00:30] Liam: Great - we'll show how our hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints work end-to-end and then jump into the Console for monitoring and Optimize suggestions. Quick ask: what's your current volume and SLOs?
[00:45] Elena: We're around 800 QPS at peak on search, 99th perc latency target is sub-250ms for first-pass results. Rerank can be a bit higher, say up to 500ms tolerated for a small subset.
[01:05] Maya: Good, that's helpful. For hosted we typically advise a hybrid pattern - fast vector search (first pass) followed by Redwood rerank for top-K. That keeps cost down.
[01:25] Tom: Is the rerank running on the same model family? Any concerns about token costs?
[01:33] Liam: We recommend a smaller embedding model for vectors (e.g., rwd-embed-small) and a compact reranker model - that's where Optimize helps with quantization and batching profiles. We'll show the Console cost breakouts in a minute.
[02:05] Raj: Cool. Show us the API request and response for embeddings first?
[02:12] Liam: Sure - here's a sample curl: POST /v1/embeddings with text payload, returns a 768-d vector. (pauses) Sorry, obvious note - vector dim depends on model selected.
[02:35] Liam: Transcript quirk: sometimes our auto-gen docs call it "embed-d" - ignore that, it's just a shorthand.
[02:50] Maya: We'll also share the SDK snippet after the call.
[03:05] Raj: Do you provide a hosted index or do we need to host our own vector DB?
[03:12] Liam: Redwood Hosted API returns embeddings; we don't lock you into a DB. Common patterns: push embeddings to Pinecone/Weaviate/your in-house Elastic or use our partner connectors. Some customers prefer us to host simple indexes - we can discuss.
[03:40] Elena: For privacy and compliance, we need to know retention windows and whether raw text or embeddings are persisted.
[03:49] Maya: Hosted defaults: we retain short-term for debugging, but you can opt-out. Enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private can control retention and KMS keys. We'll attach the security whitepaper and the retention config doc.
[04:12] Raj: Can you do VPC peering?
[04:18] Liam: Yes - for Private deployments we do VPC options; hosted supports private network endpoints in some cloud regions. For fully on-prem, there's a Redwood Private package.
[04:35] Tom: latency numbers - what should we expect for embeddings call and rerank call?
[04:42] Liam: Embeddings are typically 20-80ms depending on model & region, rerank depends on model size - small reranker ~50-200ms; across larger models higher. We'll run a benchmark against your sample corpus.
[05:05] Raj: How does the rerank endpoint work? Is it a single API that accepts query + candidate docs?
[05:12] Liam: Exactly: POST /v1/rerank with query and list of candidate snippets or ids; it returns scores and optionally reordered results. We also support cross-encoder and pairwise modes. Implementation note: for large K you want to use candidate filters first.
[05:40] Elena: Does it support embeddings-only rerank or full-text rerank?
[05:45] Liam: Both; embeddings-based re-scoring is cheaper, full cross-encoder rerank gives better quality but higher latency & token cost. Optimize can recommend thresholds.
[06:05] Maya: Let's jump into the Console - Liam, can you share your screen?
[06:12] [screen share begins]
[06:18] Liam: Here is the Routes tab - you can see per-route token cost, average latency, and tail latencies. That's where you can set per-route SLOs and fallbacks. Note: the transcription sometimes shows "routes" as "roots" in exported logs.
[06:40] Raj: Nice, I see a cost breakdown by model and by API call. Is there a way to pin a model version?
[06:47] Liam: Yes - pinning is available per-route. That helps with predictable latency during rollouts.
[07:05] Elena: Any hooks for tracing? We use Jaeger.
[07:10] Liam: We emit tracing headers and can integrate with your tracing backend; Raven - I mean, Redwood - sorry, brain slip - we can attach examples.
[07:30] Tom: How do you handle KV cache across rerank calls? I recall some docs about KV cache for decoder models.
[07:38] Liam: Good question - KV cache is mostly for autoregressive generation; for rerank cross-encoders there's less opportunity. For chat/generation flows we can preserve KV cache and warm prefixes to reduce latency.
[07:58] Raj: Let's talk about cost controls - we need a predictable model to forecast spend.
[08:05] Maya: We have per-route quotas, batch-size caps, and the Optimize tool suggests quantization and batching profiles to reduce token/compute cost. For example, quantizing a reranker to 4-bit can cut costs by ~40% in some workloads.
[08:28] Elena: What's the tradeoff on quality?
[08:30] Liam: Small drop in NDCG in some datasets; Optimize uses evals to flag regressions against your holdout prompt set. We'll run evals on your benchmark to validate.
[08:55] Raj: Any customers using hosted for production with PHI or sensitive data?
[09:02] Maya: A handful, mostly on Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted can be configured with stricter retention and customer-managed KMS in some cases, but for heavy compliance we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[09:25] Tom: You mentioned fallbacks earlier - can we implement automatic fallback to a cheaper model if capacity is constrained?
[09:32] Liam: Yes - Smart routing policies allow fallback by cost/latency/region and can be per-route.
[09:45] Raj: Show us a sample rerank request and response in the Console logs.
[09:52] Liam: Here - request payload includes query, candidates array, optional metadata, and response includes scores, normalized. Note: logging will mask PII by default if enabled. Sometimes the auto-transcript shows "mask PII" as "mask pie" so ignore typos.
[10:20] Elena: For integration, do you provide batch rerank endpoints? We have large nightly reorders for recommendations.
[10:27] Liam: Yes, batch endpoints exist; also streaming options for large jobs. We'll include throughput guidance for Dedicated capacity.
[10:45] Raj: Competitors - are you claiming better latency than Pinecone or better rerank quality than in-house?
[10:53] Maya: We don't claim one-size-fits-all - our differentiation is the unified runtime + tooling: transparent metrics per-token, Optimize suggestions, and fallbacks that make production behavior predictable. We'll share benchmark guidelines and a sample spreadsheet.
[11:20] Tom: Security checklist - SOC2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS - all supported?
[11:28] Maya: Yes - SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private/Dedicated. We'll share the security pack link.
[11:45] Raj: Great. Can we do a short PoC: 2-week benchmark using our search traffic?
[11:52] Liam: Absolutely - typical PoC runs 1-2 weeks: ingest sample documents, run first-pass vector search + rerank, collect metrics. We'll help with a benchmark harness.
[12:10] Elena: For the harness, what's required from our side?
[12:15] Liam: A sample corpus (10-100k docs), a query log or synthetic queries, and target metrics (latency, NDCG). We'll provide the harness and scripts.
[12:32] Raj: Any gotchas with tokenization? Our docs are multi-lingual - Spanish, Portuguese.
[12:38] Liam: Model tokenizers vary; embeddings models we recommend have robust multi-lingual support; we'll validate on a subset.
[12:55] Maya: Quick demo: run a live rerank - I'll hand to Liam to post a sample with real snippets.
[13:05] Liam: Posting request... (typing) - here's a query "best weekend getaways" and 10 candidates - rerank returns reordered list with scores.
[13:30] Raj: Looks solid. How does caching for repeated queries work?
[13:36] Liam: We have prefix/KV caching for generation, and prefix caching for common embeddings - plus an LRU for identical queries to reduce duplicate compute.
[13:58] Elena: Do you provide per-tenant isolation for embeddings vectors? We can't have cross-customer leakage.
[14:05] Maya: Absolutely - strict tenant isolation; embeddings never mixed across customers in hosted indexes. We'll include the architecture diagram.
[14:28] Raj: For the PoC, can we use hosted and then move to Dedicated if needed?
[14:33] Maya: Yes - many customers start hosted and shift to Dedicated or Private with a config change; the API surface remains the same so minimal code changes.
[14:50] Tom: Any rate limits we should be aware of?
[14:55] Liam: Default quotas are conservative for new accounts; for pilots we bump them and for Dedicated you get reserved throughput.
[15:12] Raj: Pricing - can we get a sense now?
[15:17] Maya: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet, but high level: embeddings per-1k units, rerank per-request plus token charges for cross-encoder. Dedicated has monthly reserved GPU pricing.
[15:34] Elena: Is there a free tier for initial testing?
[15:37] Maya: Yes - credits for trial and a sandbox project.
[15:50] Raj: Any limitations on document size for rerank?
[15:56] Liam: There are payload size limits; for large docs we recommend chunking and candidate pruning.
[16:12] Maya: Now I'll show Optimize suggestions: batching profiles, recommended quantization, and a sample eval result indicating model swap candidates.
[16:20] [screen shows Optimize UI]
[16:30] Liam: Optimize flagged that for your workload we could batch small queries up to 8 and quantize the reranker to 4-bit with a negligible drop on our eval set. We'll run this on your dataset to verify.
[16:55] Raj: How about monitoring regressions?
[17:00] Liam: Optimize integrates with per-prompt evals and alerts on dropped NDCG or increased hallucination rates; you can set thresholds and automatic rollback.
[17:18] Elena: Great - do you keep historical model outputs for audits?
[17:24] Maya: We retain outputs per your retention policy; for audit you can export logs or keep them in your S3 via connector.
[17:40] Raj: Any examples of customers who migrated to Dedicated for cost reasons?
[17:45] Maya: A few large marketplaces moved to Dedicated to get better unit economics and reserved throughput. We'll share anonymized case studies.
[18:05] Tom: For onboarding, what support do you include?
[18:10] Maya: AE+SE-led kickoff, integration docs, a short runbook for benchmark, and optional paid SRE hours for dedicated setups.
[18:30] Raj: Ok, action items and next steps then.
[18:36] Maya: Recap - we'll send pricing, security pack, benchmark harness, and propose dates for kickoff. Liam will own the benchmark setup.
[18:50] Elena: Sounds good. Also please include a sample PoC plan for 2 weeks.
[19:00] Liam: Noted.
[19:05] [minor crosstalk]
[19:15] Tom: A couple quick questions - do you support SAML with SCIM provisioning?
[19:22] Maya: Yes to both, SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise accounts.
[19:30] Raj: Any SLA on hosted?
[19:32] Maya: Hosted has a best-effort SLA; Dedicated offers contractual SLA with uptime and latency SLOs.
[19:50] Elena: How long to spin up Dedicated capacity?
[19:55] Liam: Depends on region and SKU, generally a few days to a couple of weeks for full provisioning.
[20:12] Raj: Last question - do you support on-prem air-gapped for legal/regulatory reasons?
[20:18] Maya: Yes - Redwood Private is our on-prem option for air-gapped deployments.
[20:30] Tom: Okay thanks, that's helpful.
[20:35] Maya: We'll follow up with the docs and the pricing. Anything else?
[20:42] Raj: No, that's it. Looking forward to the PoC.
[20:48] Maya: Great - thanks all.
[20:52] [meeting end recorded at 16:48 UTC]
